'''''Nyana rooiwalensis''''' is an [[extinct]] species of early [[massopoda]]n [[sauropodomorph]] dinosaur known from the [[Late Triassic]] ([[Norian]]–[[Rhaetian]] ages) [[Elliot Formation]] of South Africa. It is the [[Monotypic taxon|only species]] in the genus '''''Nyana''''', and is known from a partial articulated skull and associated fragmentary skeleton of a juvenile individual.

== Discovery and naming ==
The ''Nyana'' fossil material was discovered in 2018 in outcrops of the lower [[Elliot Formation]] in [[Eastern Cape Province]], South Africa. The specimen is housed in the [[Evolutionary Studies Institute]], where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen BP/1/8468. It consists of a partial skeleton of a juvenile individual, comprising much of an articulated skull, several vertebrae, and parts of the forelimb and hindlimb.<ref name="Nyana" />

In 2026, Atashni Moopen and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Nyana rooiwalensis'' as a new genus and species of sauropodomorph dinosaur based on these fossil remains, designating BP/1/8468 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Nyana'', is a word meaning {{gloss|son}} or {{gloss|child}} in [[Xhosa language|Xhosa]], as well as {{gloss|small}} in [[Sesotho]]. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''rooiwalensis'', references the discovery of the only known specimen in Rooiwal.<ref name="Nyana" />
